2027-02-22.title: The Chair of St Peter, Apostle
readings: As an elder myself, I exhort the elders: tend the flock of God
The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want
You are Peter, and to you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven
2027-02-22.alt: Feast. The readings of Monday of the Second Week of Lent give way to those of the feast. The Gloria is said; the Gospel acclamation is sung without Alleluia, as throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-02-22.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: In the second week of Lent the Church pauses for a feast of white: the Chair of St Peter. A chair seems a strange thing to celebrate. But in the ancient world the cathedra was the seat from which a teacher taught and a bishop presided; Jesus himself speaks of the scribes who “sit on Moses' seat” (Matthew 23:2). Since at least the fourth century the Church of Rome has kept this day in honour of Peter's chair, that is, of the mission Christ gave him to teach, to guide and to hold the Church together in one faith. We do not honour a piece of wood. We honour the Lord, who chose a fisherman and made him a rock, and who still keeps his Church united around Peter's successor.

The Gospel takes us to Caesarea Philippi, far in the north, where a great rock face rose above a shrine to pagan gods. There Jesus asks two questions. First: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” The answers are generous but not enough: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, a prophet. Then the question that no one can answer for us: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon speaks for all: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” Jesus tells him that this faith is a gift: “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven.” Then he gives Simon a new name. “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” In Aramaic the name and the rock are the same word, Kepha. He gives him the keys of the kingdom, the sign of a steward over the king's house, as Isaiah once said of Eliakim: “he shall open, and no one shall shut.” And he gives the power to bind and to loose.

Peter did not become a rock by his own strength. The same chapter tells how he tried to turn Jesus away from the cross and heard the words “Get behind me, Satan!” Later he denied his Master three times. His firmness comes from the prayer of Jesus: “I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.” That is why the first reading sounds so humble. The old Apostle writes as “an elder myself and a witness of the sufferings of Christ,” and asks the shepherds to tend the flock “not under compulsion but willingly,” not lording it over others but being examples, until “the chief shepherd appears.” The Psalm names that chief Shepherd: “The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.” In Lent this feast reminds us that conversion is never private. We return to God within the one flock, under the one Shepherd, held together by the faith Peter confessed.
conn: A town at the foot of Mount Hermon, near a cave and rock face where Pan was worshipped. Against that rock of false gods Jesus names the true rock.
Jesus spoke Aramaic; Kepha means rock. Greek turned it into Petros. Paul often calls him Cephas (Galatians 2:9; 1 Corinthians 15:5).
Isaiah 22:22 describes the steward of the royal house receiving the key of the house of David. The keys mean authority given in trust, on behalf of the king.

Rabbinic terms for deciding what is permitted and forbidden, and for admitting to or excluding from the community. Christ gives this authority to Peter, and later to the apostles together (Matthew 18:18).

Cathedra means seat of teaching; a cathedral is the church where the bishop's chair stands. In St Peter's Basilica, Bernini's bronze Chair (1666) encloses an ancient wooden chair venerated as a relic.

A Roman list of feasts from the year 354 already marks 22 February for Peter's chair. The day was also linked with the old Roman custom of honouring the dead of one's family: the Church honoured her father in the faith.
altar: At every Mass the Pope is named in the Eucharistic Prayer, together with our bishop. We are praying in communion with Peter.
The Shepherd who spreads a table for us (Psalm 23:5) feeds his flock with his own Body, and the unity of the Church is both shown and made at the altar.

Authority given in trust, for service.

live: Today, in your own words, tell Jesus who he is for you.
Pray the Our Father and a Hail Mary for the Holy Father, that his faith may not fail.
Pray for your bishop and priests
Name your bishop and parish priest in prayer, and thank them for one thing.
Where there is division in your family or parish, take one step toward peace this week.
fathers: The Lord built the Church upon one, so that unity might be shown from its source. Whoever abandons the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded cannot be sure he is in the Church.
The firmness that Peter received from Christ the Rock passes on to his heirs. Wherever his successor teaches in faith, Peter is still at work, strengthening his brothers.
Where Peter is, there is the Church; and where the Church is, there is not death but life eternal.
magis: Peter's confession, the rock and the keys: the power to bind and loose.
The college of bishops and its head, the Roman Pontiff, the perpetual source of unity.
The Pope, Bishop of Rome and successor of Peter.
Vatican II: Peter's successor as the visible foundation of the unity of faith and communion.
Christ the Good Shepherd and the ministry of shepherds in his Church.
saints: Fisherman of Bethsaida and Capernaum, called by Jesus, named Rock, first among the Twelve. He led the Church in Jerusalem and later in Rome, where he was crucified under Nero about AD 64 and buried on the Vatican Hill.
23 Feb: St Polycarp (commemoration). 24–26 Feb: Lenten weekdays. 27 Feb: St Gregory of Narek (commemoration). 28 Feb: Third Sunday of Lent; First Scrutiny of the elect.
2027-02-22.prayer: Grant, we pray, almighty God, that no tempests may disturb us, for you have set us fast on the rock of the Apostle Peter's confession of faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Son of the living God, you built your Church on Peter. Keep our Holy Father strong in faith and gentle in love; bless our bishop and priests; and make us one flock, faithful to you through this Lent and always. Amen.

quick: Peter confessed Jesus as the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
Jesus named him Rock and gave him the keys of the kingdom.
Peter's successor still strengthens the Church in one faith.
2027-02-22.action: Pray today for the Pope and for your bishop by name.
2027-02-22.question: If Jesus asked me today, “Who do you say that I am?”, what would I honestly answer?
catechism: Peter's confession and the keys of the kingdom.
The Pope, successor of Peter, source of unity.
The Church, the flock of the one Shepherd.
kidsaint: A fisherman who loved Jesus very much, but sometimes was afraid and made mistakes. Once he even said he did not know Jesus! But Jesus forgave him and made him the leader of the apostles. Lesson: Jesus can make us strong, even when we are weak.
2027-02-22.special: The Chair of St Peter, Apostle. Feast in Lent: Gloria said, no Alleluia.
term: The bishop's chair, a sign of his office of teaching and shepherding. The church where it stands is the cathedral. The Chair of Peter stands for the teaching office of the Pope.

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say I am? Peter answered: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God! Jesus was happy and said: you are Peter, the rock. I will build my Church on you. Today the Pope takes Peter's place and helps the whole Church stay together.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and our bishop.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is Jesus for each one of us? Let everyone say one thing.”

illus: A teacher in a Kottayam school showed her class a photo of the great bronze Chair in St Peter's Basilica. One boy said: but nobody sits in it! She smiled: exactly. It is too big for anyone. It reminds every Pope that he only keeps the seat for Jesus, and that his strength comes from Christ's prayer, not his own.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the living God, you built your Church on the rock of Peter. Keep us united in faith and love. Amen.

You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church (Matthew 16:18). How do I love and pray for the Church?
Tend the flock of God… willingly (1 Peter 5:2). Whom am I called to care for?
pm.resp: The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
interc: For our Holy Father the Pope, that the Lord may keep his faith firm.
For our bishop and all the shepherds of the Church.
For Christians who are divided, that we may be one.
For those who are losing their faith, that someone may strengthen them.
For our group, that we may confess Jesus with Peter's faith.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the middle of Lent we put on white and celebrate the Chair of St Peter. We do not honour a chair. We honour the mission Christ gave to a fisherman: to teach, to guide and to hold the Church together in one faith.

At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked: who do people say that the Son of Man is? Many answers, all too small. Then: but who do you say that I am? (Matthew 16:15). This question comes to each of us. No one can answer it for us.

Simon answered: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. And Jesus said: flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven. Faith is a gift. Then he gave him a new name: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it (Matthew 16:18).

Peter was not strong by nature. He tried to keep Jesus from the cross. He denied him three times. But Jesus prayed for him, that his faith would not fail, and told him: strengthen your brothers. The rock is made by grace.

That is why the first reading is so humble. Peter, an old man, calls himself an elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and asks shepherds to tend the flock willingly, not lording it over others but being examples (1 Peter 5:2–3). Authority in the Church is service.

Today let us pray for our Holy Father, for our bishop, for our priests. And let us answer the question of Jesus with Peter's words, from our hearts: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus gave Simon a new name: Peter, which means rock! Peter was not always brave, but Jesus made him strong and made him the leader of his Church.
Today the Pope helps the Church like Peter did. Let us say a Hail Mary for the Pope today!
